ambiguities: Whether notes are organized in folders that should map to site sections or whether navigation is primarily tag/backlink-driven.
Whether to support multiple vaults/repos or a single notes directory.
Whether to generate a backlinks panel per page, a global graph view, or both.
Whether to support note aliases (multiple titles pointing to one note) and how to expose them.
Whether to treat headings as linkable targets and how to generate stable heading anchors.
Whether unpublished/draft notes exist and how to exclude them (frontmatter flag, folder rule).
Whether to preserve raw Markdown display (code fences, callouts) exactly as in the editor or allow formatting differences.
Whether to support mobile-friendly UI and accessibility requirements beyond basic responsive layout.

avenues_considered.summary: Adopt an existing static site generator (e.g., Eleventy/Hugo/Astro) and add plugins/pipelines for tags, backlinks, and search.
Build a purpose-made Markdown-to-static-site generator focused on note-taking features (wikilinks, backlinks, graph, tag pages).
Use a docs framework (e.g., Docusaurus/MkDocs) and extend it for wikilinks/backlinks and note-oriented navigation.
Generate mostly raw content and rely on a client-side app for navigation/search (SPA-like shell + prebuilt JSON index).
Prioritize a strong search/indexing pipeline (FlexSearch/Lunr/Meilisearch-hosted) and keep page rendering simple.

candidate_approaches: Eleventy + markdown-it: parse Markdown, add a wikilinks/backlinks plugin, generate tag index pages, use FlexSearch for client-side search.
Hugo: use shortcodes/partials for backlinks and taxonomies for tags; generate a JSON search index for Lunr/FlexSearch.
Astro: render Markdown/MDX pages, build a search index at build time, implement backlinks via a preprocessing pass over the content graph.
Custom Node/Python generator: two-pass build (parse notes -> build link graph -> render templates), output static HTML + JSON index.
MkDocs Material: leverage nav and search plugin, extend with a preprocessing step to translate wikilinks and generate backlinks sections.
default_assumptions: Input notes are local Markdown files in a single root directory with optional YAML frontmatter.
Static output should work on purely static hosting (no server-side runtime required).
Backlinks are derived from explicit links between notes (not from plain-text mention detection) unless extended later.
Tags are sourced from YAML frontmatter (e.g., tags: [a, b]) with optional later support for inline #tags.
Wikilinks [[Note Title]] are supported and resolved by filename/title with a deterministic disambiguation rule.
Search runs fully client-side using a prebuilt index shipped with the site.
Build tooling should be cross-platform and runnable via a single CLI command.

key_decisions.summary: Choose foundation: extend an existing SSG vs build a custom generator.
Define wikilink syntax and resolution rules (by filename, title, frontmatter id/slug; disambiguation strategy).
Decide canonical identifiers and URL scheme (path-based, slug-based, ID-based) and redirect strategy on rename.
Choose tag source(s) and normalization (frontmatter vs inline; hierarchical tags; casing rules).
Select search indexing approach (FlexSearch vs Lunr vs simple substring; index size and performance targets).
Determine which Markdown extensions to support (GFM, footnotes, math, mermaid, callouts) and which are out of scope initially.

impact: Build requirements for extracting link context
key_decisions.summary: Decide how backlinks are presented (inline section, sidebar panel, separate page) and whether to include context snippets.
Decide required developer experience: one-shot build only vs watch mode with incremental rebuilds.

recommended_defaults: Start with an existing SSG (Eleventy) to minimize boilerplate and leverage templating/layout ecosystem.
Support YAML frontmatter with fields: title, tags, draft, aliases, slug (optional).
Adopt wikilinks syntax [[Note Name]] with resolution priority: frontmatter.slug/id > filename stem; enforce deterministic disambiguation (e.g., prefer closest path, else error report).
Perform a two-pass build: (1) parse all notes and extract links/tags/metadata, (2) render pages with backlinks and tag pages.
Use FlexSearch (client-side) with a prebuilt JSON index containing title, tags, url, and content excerpt; keep index minimal for size.
Generate per-note backlinks section listing referring notes (title + link), with optional future enhancement for context snippets.
Default URL scheme: /notes/<slug-or-path>/ with stable slug generation; include a build-time report for broken links and duplicates.
Ship as a CLI: build, serve (static preview), and optionally watch; target zero-server static hosting compatibility.

uncertainties.summary: Number of notes, average size, and total repository size (impacts build time, indexing strategy, and hosting constraints).
Desired link syntax and resolution rules (e.g., [[wikilinks]] vs Markdown links, case sensitivity, path ambiguity, aliases).
Markdown features needed (GFM tables, footnotes, math, mermaid, callouts) and how strictly to support Obsidian-style extensions.
How tags are defined (frontmatter, inline #tags, both) and normalization rules (hierarchical tags, casing, spaces).
What qualifies as a backlink (only explicit links, also mentions, headings/anchors, transclusions/embeds).
Search expectations (full-text vs title-only, fuzzy matching, highlighting, ranking, offline support, multi-language stemming).
Preferred URL scheme (based on file paths, slugs, note IDs) and long-term stability/redirect needs.
Hosting environment and constraints (GitHub Pages, Netlify, self-hosted; CI limits; need for zero server).
Need for incremental builds/watch mode speed vs acceptable full rebuild times.
How to handle attachments (images/PDFs), relative paths, and link rewrites during build.
